title: Minimal Container Runtime (Docker-like) in Go
problem: Container management platforms like Docker and Kubernetes rely fundamentally on standard Linux kernel primitives—namespaces, control groups (cgroups v2), and chroot/pivot_root filesystem mounts—wrapped beneath friendly command-line utilities. Operating containers without understanding these low-level abstractions obscures critical boundaries regarding isolation guarantees, memory leak remediation, resource limit enforcement, and root escape vectors. This project implements a minimal OCI-compliant container runtime from scratch in Go that forks child processes into isolated PID, mount, UTS, and network namespaces, configures cgroups v2 memory and CPU ceilings, and pivots into an isolated root filesystem.
use_cases: Secure sandbox process execution for untrusted multi-tenant code runners
Lightweight edge container execution environments with minimal memory footprint
Container security research and kernel-level isolation vulnerability assessment
hard_parts: Executing Linux system calls (clone, setns, unshare, pivot_root) cleanly in Go without runtime thread corruption
Interfacing with cgroups v2 unified filesystem hierarchy across memory.max, cpu.max, and pids.max controllers
Safely unmounting host filesystems and isolating device nodes (/dev, /proc, /sys) to prevent container breakouts
Managing process synchronization across parent and child processes prior to namespace activation
screener_signals: Clean systems-level Go codebase making direct syscalls to Linux kernel primitives
Demonstrated PID 1 isolation inside the container with 0 host processes visible via ps
Kernel-enforced cgroups v2 memory limit verification triggering the Linux OOM killer on rogue allocations

components.name: Process Namespace Isolator
components.purpose: Invokes clone and unshare syscalls to establish isolated PID, UTS, IPC, and mount namespaces

components.name: cgroups v2 Controller
components.purpose: Creates unified control group directories and writes memory.max, cpu.max, and pids.max limits

components.name: Rootfs Mount & Pivot Engine
components.purpose: Mounts private proc/sys filesystems and executes pivot_root into an isolated rootfs directory

components.name: Container Lifecycle CLI
components.purpose: Provides run, exec, and ps subcommands managing container execution and exit codes

architecture.data_flow: User invokes the runtime CLI passing an Alpine rootfs and a command; the runtime creates a new cgroups v2 group with configured resource ceilings; the Go runtime re-executes itself via /proc/self/exe with clone flags (CLONE_NEWPID, CLONE_NEWNS, CLONE_NEWUTS); child process assigns its PID to cgroup.procs; the child pivots rootfs into target directory; procfs mounts to /proc; the target command executes as PID 1.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Linux kernel cgroups v2 kills processes exceeding memory.max; PID namespace restricts signal dispatch to container child processes.

targets.method: Inspection of process table (/proc) from inside container versus host process table
targets.input: Containerized execution of ps -ef inside isolated Alpine rootfs
targets.environment: Linux kernel 5.15+ (Ubuntu 22.04 LTS / Debian 12 / WSL2 with cgroups v2), root/sudo permissions
targets.minimum_pass: Target process observes PID 1 and can view 0 host processes from inside namespace
targets.target: Target process observes PID 1 and can view 0 host processes from inside namespace
targets.report: Container terminal output log comparing internal and external ps results

targets.metric: cgroups v2 Memory Limit Kernel Enforcement
targets.method: Execution of memory allocation program allocating 100MB against a 64MB memory.max limit
targets.input: Compiled Go memory-eater script allocating slices in an infinite loop
targets.environment: Linux kernel 5.15+ with unified cgroups v2 hierarchy
targets.minimum_pass: Container process terminated by kernel OOM killer within 500ms of exceeding limit
targets.target: Container process terminated by kernel OOM killer within 150ms of exceeding limit
targets.report: Kernel dmesg log and cgroup memory.events file showing oom_kill counter increment

targets.method: Measurement of wall-clock time from CLI invocation to interactive shell prompt readiness
targets.input: CLI run command launching /bin/sh inside minimal Alpine Linux rootfs
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, local ext4 filesystem
targets.minimum_pass: Container shell boots and responds to command in < 250ms
targets.target: Container shell boots and responds to command in < 120ms
targets.report: Benchmark execution timing log averaging 20 consecutive container launches

prerequisites: Intermediate Go programming (syscall package, os/exec, process handling)
Familiarity with Linux operating system concepts (file descriptors, signals, procfs)
Access to a Linux environment (native Linux, WSL2, or a Linux virtual machine)

environment.os: Linux (native Ubuntu/Debian/Fedora or Windows WSL2 with cgroups v2 enabled)
environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU and kernel systems programming)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: Root or sudo privileges required on local Linux machine to manage namespaces and cgroups
environment.reference_environment: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS x86_64 or ARM64 with Go 1.21+ and sudo privileges
environment.fallback_path: Local disposable Linux VM using Multipass, Vagrant, or VirtualBox if host OS does not support native namespaces

riskiest_component.name: pivot_root System Call Failure on Shared Mount Points
riskiest_component.fallback: Execute mount make-rprivate on the host root mount before invoking pivot_root to eliminate shared mount propagation errors

deliverables: Git repository containing Go runtime source code, syscall wrappers, and CLI subcommands
Minimal Alpine Linux rootfs provisioning script
Automated test suite verifying PID isolation, cgroups memory caps, and pivot_root security
Screener verification script running end-to-end container execution in under 2 minutes
out_of_scope: Docker Image tarball layer downloading and OCI image registry pulling
Multi-host overlay networking across distributed nodes
safety_note: Requires root or sudo privileges to invoke Linux namespace and cgroup system calls. Execute inside a virtual machine or disposable developer environment.
resources: Linux Programmer's Manual namespaces(7) and cgroups(7) documentation
Liz Rice - Building a Container from Scratch in Go architecture reference
Open Container Initiative (OCI) Runtime Specification standard

rubric.action: Execute command and inspect process table output
rubric.expected_result: ps command shows only PID 1 (/bin/ps) and no host background processes
rubric.pass_criterion: Output contains only 1 running process with PID 1 and returns exit code 0

rubric.action: Execute memory stress program that attempts to allocate 100MB
rubric.expected_result: Kernel cgroups v2 detects limit breach and sends SIGKILL to process
rubric.evidence_location: Terminal output reporting 'Killed' and cgroup memory.events log
rubric.pass_criterion: Process terminates with exit code 137 and memory.events reports oom_kill count >= 1

rubric.action: Inspect mounts visible inside container root filesystem
rubric.expected_result: Only private container mounts are listed; host root filesystem is unmounted and inaccessible
rubric.evidence_location: Terminal output log of container mounts
rubric.pass_criterion: Host root mount absent from list and exit code 0

rubric.input: Timing benchmark running 20 consecutive container invocations
rubric.expected_result: Benchmark calculates mean container startup latency from invocation to exit
rubric.pass_criterion: Average startup latency is < 250ms across 20 consecutive runs

rubric.input: Dynamic custom hostname generated at runtime by verification script
rubric.expected_result: Container sets hostname in isolated UTS namespace; host hostname remains untouched
rubric.evidence_location: Verification console output comparing host and container hostnames
rubric.pass_criterion: Container reports dynamic hostname and host reports original hostname with exit code 0

worksheet.q1: The student builds a minimal container runtime in Go using Linux namespaces (PID, mount, UTS), cgroups v2 unified resource limits, and rootfs pivot_root isolation.
worksheet.q2: Core path: namespace isolation, cgroups v2 memory/CPU limits, pivot_root mount isolation, and lifecycle CLI (34h). Extended path: veth network pairs and rootless user namespaces (+15h).
worksheet.q3: Components: Namespaces (8h), cgroups v2 (5h), pivot_root (5h), CLI (5h), Integration Tests (4h), Docs & Buffer (3h). Total 30h x 1.15 = 34.5 -> 34h.
worksheet.q4: Project types: Systems/low-level/networking. Metrics: PID Namespace Isolation, Memory Limit Enforcement, Shell Boot Latency. Rejected: web-service RPS throughput.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: Linux syscall execution in Go, cgroups v2 unified controller hierarchy, pivot_root shared mount traps, and process synchronization.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: minimal Alpine Linux rootfs (5MB) and memory stress-test binary. No personal data.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux with cgroups v2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost. Requires sudo. Fallback: disposable Linux VM (Multipass/VirtualBox).
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: pivot_root shared mount failure. Fallback: make host mount rprivate before pivot.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: mocked shell script. Anti-fake check 5 validates dynamic hostname setting inside UTS namespace while confirming host hostname is unmodified.
